To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) the short-term interest rates are important in explaining the speculative single-family housing starts, (b) the short-term rates are important in the housing starts equation even when the monetary base is included in the regression, (c) there is evidence that the speculative housing starts equation is unstable, and (d) the instability is due primarily to the short-term interest-rate variable and to the monetary base.
the speculative housing starts, which are the main source of supply of housing units, are highly sensitive to changes in interest rate and monetary base.

(1) the speculative sector of housing starts has a strong short-run response to interest rate changes; (2) the speculative sector responds positively to the monetary base; (3) the speculative sector does not respond to the long-run interest rate; and (4) the speculative sector is not affected by the price of housing.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the short-term dynamics of the speculative housing starts.
the short-run dynamics of the speculative sector and its impact on the housing starts.
the short-run behavior of the speculative housing starts.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the speculative sector is a source of supply which is sensitive to interest rate changes and that this sector is not a source of instability in single-family housing starts in the short-run.
the speculative housing starts in single-family housing are highly sensitive to the short-run changes in the monetary policy and the short-term interest rates.
the speculative sector is a significant source of supply of housing units, and that it is affected by monetary policy.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the speculative housing starts can be viewed as a component of the inventory of new houses, and that this component can be modeled in a similar fashion to the inventory of durable goods.
the speculative housing starts, as an indicator of the short-run housing starts, are not a good leading indicator for the long-run housing starts.
the monetary base is a significant factor in the speculative housing starts and, in addition, that the speculative housing sector is an important source of supply of housing units.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the speculative sector is highly unstable and is a source of instability of the housing market as a whole.
a significant part of the speculative housing starts can be explained by the short-run fluctuations in the monetary policy.
a monetary shock has a significant impact on the speculative sector of single-family housing starts, which in turn affects the housing market as a whole.
